scope: Proposition 3.4 of the manuscript “Hamiltonian Fixed Points Below the Stable Morse Number in Dimension Twenty-Two” (preprints/Hamiltonian-Fixed-Points-Below-the-Stable-Morse-Number-in-Dimension-Twenty-Two-October-5-2026/hamiltonian-fixed-points-below-stable-morse-number.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 347 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 12e5b850a5797391), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 9. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every integer m ≥ 1 there is a simply connected closed Kähler manifold Xm of complex dimension nine, obtained by blowing up CP9 along m disjoint copies of each of Z2 and Z3. Its integral homology is Hi(Xm; Z) ∼ = Hi(CP9 ; Z) ⊕ 6 M r=1 Hi−2r(Z2; Z) !⊕m ⊕ 4 M r=1 Hi−2r(Z3; Z) !⊕m . (3.7)
